reason: The cited evidence does not address HfNbTiVAl10, its hierarchical heterostructure, or the specific microstructural descriptors proposed. E1 and E2 report tensile properties of different RHEAs without microstructural descriptor quantification. E3 shows ML prediction of yield strength in other alloys but not for the target material or fracture behavior. E4 and E5 discuss fracture properties of different alloy/glass systems, providing no support for the claimed speed or accuracy gains over DFT/atomistic simulations for this material.
premises: Microstructural descriptors (phase fractions, misfit volumes, lattice distortion) can be quantified for HfNbTiVAl10's hierarchical heterostructure.
These descriptors correlate with Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture behavior via strengthening mechanisms.
A machine learning surrogate model can capture these correlations to predict properties.
The surrogate model will be ~10× faster than DFT/atomistic simulations.
Prediction errors will be within 15–20% of experimental values, improving on DFT/atomistic baselines.
